newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees 1997 economic growth at 7.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees 1997 economic growth at 7.9 pct.

text.p: Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said on Saturday Indonesia had a healthy economic outlook for 1997, with growth estimated at 7.9 percent and inflation at around six percent.
"We expect our economy development in 1997 will better than 1996 and the prospect is bright. Economic growth is expected to be around 7.9 percent and inflation around six percent in 1997," he said.

Addressing a one-day economic seminar organised by the ruling Golkar party, he said the government estimated economic growth in 1996 at between 7.6 percent and 7.9 percent, compared with 8.07 percent in 1995.
He said inflation in 1996 was estimated at between 6.5 percent and 6.8 percent, compared with 8.64 percent in 1995.

Ginanjar said growth in the agriculture sector would slow in 1996. He estimated agricultural growth at between 1.9 percent and 2.3 percent, compared with 4.2 growth in 1995, due to a slowdown in growth in rice production.
He said industry sector was expected to grow at between 10.9 percent and 11.4 percent in 1996, compared with 10.8 percent in 1995.
Ginanjar predicted the mining sector would grow between 6.0 percent and 6.3 percent in 1996, compared with 6.7 percent in 1995.
He said growth in houshold consumption was expected to slow to between 7.0 percent and 7.4 percent in 1996 from 8.3 percent in 1995.
Ginanjar said the government would continue to follow prudent economic policies in 1997 to control inflation and reduce the current accound deficit.

Indonesia has estimated its current account deficit would widen to $8.7 billion in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), or about four percent of gross domestic product (GDP), from $7.0 billion, or about 3.2 percent of GDP, in 1995/96.
